requirements.text: Please create an incident for Barbara ... and handle this as a moderate-priority request
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101' AND caller_id = 'USER_025' AND channel = 'phone' AND impact = 'medium' AND urgency = 'medium' AND priority = 'moderate' AND status = 'new'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (INC_100 is the highest incident id)
Barbara Perry is USER_025, the only user of that name
channel phone because the request says Barbara called
priority moderate is the request's own words; the policy's matrix gives moderate for medium x medium, low x high and high x low
impact medium and urgency medium kept from the benchmark check; the request fixes only the priority
status new is the policy's default for a new incident; the request asks for no transition

requirements.text: make sure that KB is available right away for the support team to reference
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM knowledge WHERE knowledge_id = 'KB_023' AND state = 'published'
assumptions: the article titled New HR Portal Guide is KB_023, owned by Robin Monroe (USER_031)
available means state published, the state in which the policy makes an article searchable
weak: KB_023 is already published on the seed, so the request needs no change to it

disagreement: kind: A change, B stay; chose change because the request asks for the article to be made available (a state to reach, not a forbidden change or a selector boundary), and a change already met on the seed is recorded as weak

requirements.text: make sure that KB is available right away for the support team to reference and resolve this fast
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_knowledge WHERE incident_kb_id = 'IKB_046' AND incident_id = 'INC_101' AND knowledge_id = 'KB_023' AND used_as = 'suggested'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (IKB_045 is the highest link id); the task creates exactly one link
the policy requires a knowledge search when an incident is created, with matching articles linked as used_as = suggested; the request names KB_023 as the article for this issue

Verify Incident KB link.evidence: the query passes only when no link between INC_101 and KB_023 exists, but the policy requires matching articles to be linked as used_as = suggested when an incident is created, and the request names KB_023 as the article for this issue and asks that it be available for the support team to reference; no rule in the request or policy forbids the link, and the check already holds on the seed, where neither the incident nor any link to KB_023 exists

Verify knowledge Record.evidence: KB_023 is already in state published on the seed

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on the incident (INC_101 for USER_025, phone, medium x medium = moderate, status new), the new suggested link IKB_046 between INC_101 and KB_023, the article's published state, and all three dispositions (record kept, no-link check excluded, knowledge check weak).
disagreement: kind of the requirement that KB_023 is published: A change, B stay; chose change because the request asks for the article to be made available, which is neither a forbidden change nor a selector boundary, and a change already met on the seed is recorded as weak (logged in the requirement).
The benchmark expects no knowledge link on the new incident, plausibly because no listed tool writes incident_knowledge; that is a limit of the tool set, not a rule of the request or policy, so the file requires the suggested link the policy prescribes and records that no tool can write it.
The request's 'urgently' could suggest high urgency (low impact x high urgency also gives moderate); the benchmark's medium x medium is kept because the request fixes only the priority.
Not tested: the incident's service (no seed service matches the HR portal or Workday), short description, category and assignment, none of which the request fixes; KB_023's visibility (internal) already suits the support team.
